Access tokens expire after **1 hour**; refresh tokens after **7 days**. API-key authentication is **deprecated** (see [Deprecated endpoints](#deprecated-endpoints)).\n\n### Content type\n\n`Content-Type: application/json` is required for all `POST` / `PUT` / `PATCH` requests.\n\n### Response envelope\n\nEvery response is wrapped in a common envelope:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"success\": true,\n  \"data\": { \"...\" : \"...\" },\n  \"error\": null,\n  \"meta\": { \"request_id\": \"b2c9...\", \"timestamp\": \"2024-12-15T10:30:00Z\" }\n}\n```\n\nOn failure, `success` is `false`, `data` is `null`, and `error` is populated:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"success\": false,\n  \"data\": null,\n  \"error\": { \"code\": \"ERR_CODE\", \"message\": \"Human readable message\", \"details\": {} },\n  \"meta\": { \"request_id\": \"b2c9...\", \"timestamp\": \"2024-12-15T10:30:00Z\" }\n}\n```\n\nValidation failures (`400`) include field-specific error messages in the error details. For `500` responses, always report the `meta.request_id` to support.\n\n### Error codes\n\n> | http code | meaning |\n> |-----------|---------|\n> | `400`     | Bad request — validation failed (field-specific messages included) |\n> | `401`     | Not authenticated |\n> | `403`     | Forbidden — authenticated but not authorized |\n> | `404`     | Not found |\n> | `409`     | Conflict (e.g., duplicate dataset name) |\n> | `422`     | Unprocessable entity — business rule violation |\n> | `429`     | Rate limited — see [Troubleshooting Guide](TROUBLESHOOTING_GUIDE.md) |\n> | `500`     | Server error — include `meta.request_id` in your support request |\n\n### Rate limiting\n\nRequests are counted in per-endpoint **categories** (`standard`, `bulk`, `sync`). Every response includes:\n\n> | header                 | description                          |\n> |------------------------|--------------------------------------|\n> | `X-RateLimit-Limit`    | Maximum requests in the current window |\n> | `X-RateLimit-Remaining`| Requests remaining in the current window |\n> | `X-RateLimit-Reset`    | Unix timestamp when the window resets |\n\nSee the [Troubleshooting Guide](TROUBLESHOOTING_GUIDE.md#rate-limiting-reference) for per-tier and per-category limits.\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n## Authentication\n\n#### Obtain tokens\n\n<details>\n <summary><code>POST</code> <code><b>/auth/login</b></code> <code>(authenticate user and get tokens)</code></summary>\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name      |  type     | data type | description | required |\n> |-----------|-----------|-----------|-------------|----------|\n> | `email`   |  body     | string    | Account email address | ✅ required |\n> | `password`|  body     | string    | Account password      | ✅ required |\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type       | response                                             |\n> |-----------|--------------------|------------------------------------------------------|\n> | `200`     | `application/json` | `access_token` and `refresh_token` returned          |\n> | `400`     | `application/json` | invalid credentials                                  |\n> | `429`     | `application/json` | too many attempts                                    |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```bash\n> curl -X POST https://api.datasync.io/v2/auth/login \\\n>   -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n>   -d '{\"email\": \"user@example.com\", \"password\": \"s3cret\"}'\n> ```\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n <summary><code>POST</code> <code><b>/auth/refresh</b></code> <code>(refresh access token)</code></summary>\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name            |  type     | data type | description                     | required |\n> |-----------------|-----------|-----------|---------------------------------|----------|\n> | `refresh_token` |  body     | string    | The refresh token from login    | ✅ required |\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type       | response                    |\n> |-----------|--------------------|-----------------------------|\n> | `200`     | `application/json` | New tokens returned         |\n> | `400`     | `application/json` | Invalid token               |\n> | `401`     | `application/json` | Expired token               |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```bash\n> curl -X POST https://api.datasync.io/v2/auth/refresh \\\n>   -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n>   -d '{\"refresh_token\": \"<refresh_token>\"}'\n> ```\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n <summary><code>POST</code> <code><b>/auth/logout</b></code> <code>(invalidate |-----------|--------------------|------------|\n> | `204`     | none               | Success    |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```bash\n> curl -X POST https://api.datasync.io/v2/auth/logout \\\n>   -H \"Authorization: Bearer <access_token>\" \\\n>   -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n>   -d '{\"refresh_token\": \"<refresh_token>\"}'\n> ```\n\n</details>\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n## Datasets\n\n#### List datasets\n\n<details>\n <summary><code>GET</code> If you contact support, always include it (mandatory for `500` errors) — it lets us locate your exact request.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Escalated issues — symptoms, causes, fixes\n\n### 1.1 \"401 errors after upgrading from v2.0\" (SUP-78234)\n\n**Symptom**\n\n- Integration worked on v2.0, returns `401` after the upgrade.\n- API keys still appear valid in the dashboard.\n- Common with large deployments (e.g., dozens of microservices sharing one credential).\n\n**Cause**\n\nAPI keys were **deprecated in v2.1** in favor of JWT authentication. Keys still work during the transition period (removal is scheduled for **v3**), but services that lost valid credentials — or that never implemented token refresh — fail with `401`.\n\n**Fix**\n\n1. Confirm which credential each service sends. Key-based requests must use your existing v2.0 auth header format, unchanged.\n2. If a service sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>` with an API key, it will fail — Bearer is for **JWT access tokens** from `POST /auth/login`.\n3. For JWT: on `401`, refresh the access token (`POST /auth/refresh`) and retry once. Access tokens expire after **1 hour**.\n4. For large fleets, migrate in phases with a central token broker — full walkthrough in the [Migration Guide §2.5](MIGRATION_GUIDE_v2.0_to_v2.2.md#25-escalated-scenario--jwt-migration-breaking-our-integration-47-microservices).\n5. `/me/api-keys` still working **does** mean keys are still valid — but it's deprecated; plan removal before v3.\n\n**Diagnostic shortcut**\n\n```bash\n# If this succeeds, your credential is valid and the problem is in how a\n# specific service is sending it (or the token expired mid-flight):\ncurl -H \"Authorization: Bearer <access_token>\" https://api.datasync.io/v2/me\n```\n\n### 1.2 \"Webhook never fires when a dataset is deleted\" (SUP-78456)\n\n**Symptom**\n\nYou subscribed to `dataset.deleted` and never receive callbacks when datasets are deleted/archived — while `dataset.created` and `dataset.updated` work fine.\n\n**Cause — this is expected behavior, not a bug**\n\n- **`dataset.deleted` is not a real event.** The complete event list is:\n  - `dataset.created`\n  - `dataset.updated`\n  - `sync.completed`\n  - `sync.failed`\n- `DELETE /datasets/{id}` is a **soft delete** (it sets the dataset's `archived` flag). Because the dataset still exists, archiving fires **`dataset.updated`** — with `archived: true` in the payload.\n\n**Fix**\n\n1. Remove `dataset.deleted` from your subscription (it silently never matches).\n2. Subscribe to `dataset.updated` and branch on the `archived` flag:\n\n```python\ndef handle_webhook(payload):\n    if payload[\"event\"] == \"dataset.updated\" and payload[\"data\"].get(\"archived\"):\n        handle_archive(payload[\"data\"][\"id\"])     # your \"deletion\" logic\n```\n\n3. If you genuinely need permanent dataset destruction today, there is no API for it — archive is the deletion model.\n\n**Verify your subscription**\n\n```bash\ncurl -H \"Authorization: Bearer <access_token>\" https://api.datasync.io/v2/webhooks\n# Check that \"events\" contains only valid events, and that your secret is set\n# so deliveries carry X-Webhook-Signature.\n```\n\n### 1.3 \"Rate limits hit much faster on bulk inserts\" (SUP-78512)\n\n**Symptom**\n\nOn the Free tier (100 requests/min documented), you can only complete ~20 bulk record inserts per minute before receiving `429` — while regular `GET` requests comfortably reach 100/min.\n\n**Cause**\n\nRate limits are enforced **per endpoint category**, not just per account:\n\n- Regular reads/writes → **`standard`** category (the documented 100/min on Free).\n- `POST /datasets/{id}/records` (bulk inserts) → **`bulk`** category — a **separate, lower limit** (Free tier: **20 bulk requests/min**).\n- `POST /datasets/{id}/sync` → **`sync`** category — also separate.\n\n**Fix — design your sync jobs around the categories**\n\n```python\nimport time\n\ndef bulk_insert_throttled(dataset_id, records, max_per_minute=18):\n    for chunk in chunks(records, 1000):              # hard cap: 1000 records/request\n        resp = post(f\"{BASE}/datasets/{dataset_id}/records\", json={\"records\": chunk})\n        if resp.status_code == 429:\n            reset = int(resp.headers[\"X-RateLimit-Reset\"])\n            time.sleep(max(reset - time.time(), 1))  # wait for the window to reset\n            continue\n        remaining = resp.headers.get(\"X-RateLimit-Remaining\")\n        if remaining is not None and int(remaining) <= 1:\n            time.sleep(60)                           # avoid hitting the wall mid-batch\n```\n\nFull per-tier, per-category limits: [§2 Rate limiting reference](#2-rate-limiting-reference).\n\n---\n\n## 2. Rate limiting reference\n\n### 2.1 How it works\n\n- Limits are enforced **per account (tier)** **and per category**. A `bulk` request and a `standard` request draw from **separate budgets** — they don't exhaust each other.\n- Categories are assigned per endpoint: most endpoints are `standard`; bulk record inserts are `bulk`; sync triggers are `sync` (see the [endpoint index](API_REFERENCE.md#endpoint-index)).\n- Rate-limit headers are returned on **every** response — including `429` (this was fixed in v2.1; older versions omitted them on `429`).\n\n### 2.2 Limits by tier and category\n\n| Category | Free tier | Pro tier | Enterprise |\n|----------|-----------|----------|------------|\n| **standard** | 100 requests/min · 10,000/day | 1,000 requests/min · unlimited daily | custom |\n| **bulk** (`POST /datasets/{id}/records`) | **20 requests/min** | not published — read `X-RateLimit-Limit` | custom |\n| **sync** (`POST /datasets/{id}/sync`) | not published — read `X-RateLimit-Limit` | not published — read `X-RateLimit-Limit` | custom |\n\n> Some category/tier combinations don't have published numbers. Make one request in that category and read `X-RateLimit-Limit` from the response — that is your authoritative limit for the current window. Enterprise customers can request custom limits via support.\n\n### 2.3 Response headers\n\n| Header | Meaning |\n|--------|---------|\n| `X-RateLimit-Limit` | Max requests allowed in the current window (per category) |\n| `X-RateLimit-Remaining` | Requests left in the current window |\n| `X-RateLimit-Reset` | Unix timestamp when the window resets |\n\n### 2.4 Handling `429` correctly\n\n1. **Honor `X-RateLimit-Reset`** — sleep until that Unix timestamp, don't hammer.\n2. **Back off with exponential backoff + jitter** for repeated `429`s.\n3. **Watch `X-RateLimit-Remaining`** proactively and throttle before you hit zero — don't treat the limit as something to \"discover\".\n4. **Don't retry immediately** — an instant retry consumes another request and extends your lockout.\n5. **Separate your workers by category**: a bulk-insert worker and a read worker have independent budgets; don't serialize them behind one global semaphore based on the `standard` limit.\n6. `POST /auth/login` itself returns `429` on too many attempts — implement token refresh rather than re-logging in every request.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Common migration pitfalls (v2.0 → v2.2)\n\nDrawn from recurring support patterns:\n\n| # | Pitfall | What happens | Fix |\n|---|---------|--------------|-----|\n| 1 | Keeping API-key auth past v2.1 | `401` after upgrade | Migrate to JWT ([Migration Guide §2](MIGRATION_GUIDE_v2.0_to_v2.2.md#2-authentication-migration-api-keys--jwt)) |\n| 2 | No token-refresh logic | Works for 1 hour, then everything 401s | Refresh on 401 and retry once; access tokens live 1h, refresh tokens 7d |\n| 3 | Subscribing to `dataset.deleted` | Webhook never fires | Event doesn't exist; archive fires `dataset.updated` with `archived: true` |\n| 4 | Assuming `DELETE /datasets/{id}` destroys data | Data \"still there\" | It's a soft delete — the dataset is archived, not removed |\n| 5 | Assuming `DELETE .../records/{record_id}` is soft | Data unexpectedly gone | Record deletes **are** hard deletes |\n| 6 | `limit` > 100 on list endpoints | Fewer results than expected, or validation error | Max page size is 100; paginate with `page` |\n| 7 | Sending `filter` unencoded | `400` or ignored filter | `filter` must be **JSON-encoded** |\n| 8 | Missing `Content-Type: application/json` | `400` on POST/PUT/PATCH | Set the header on all body-carrying requests |\n| 9 | Dataset names outside 3–100 chars, or duplicates | `400` / `409` | Validate name length client-side; handle `409` (conflict) explicitly |\n| 10 | > 1000 records per bulk request | `400` | Chunk inserts to ≤ 1000 records |\n| 11 | Single-record insert loops | Slow, burns through the `bulk` budget | Batch arrays (now 3x faster in v2.2) |\n| 12 | Treating all endpoints as one rate budget | Unexpected `429` on bulk/sync endpoints | Categories are separate — see §2 |\n| 13 | Polling `GET /jobs/{job_id}` in a tight loop | Wasted quota; possible rate limit | Poll with backoff, or use `sync.completed`/`sync.failed` webhooks |\n| 14 | Syncing with `mode: full` on a schedule | Massive redundant transfers | Use `mode: incremental` (v2.1+); reserve `full` for first run/repairs |\n| 15 | Parsing the response as a bare payload | Code breaks on error responses | All responses use the `{success, data, error, meta}` envelope |\n| 16 | Ignoring `error.details` on `400` | Hard-to-debug validation failures | Field-specific messages are in the error details |\n| 17 | Reporting errors without `request_id` | Slow support turnaround | Always send `meta.request_id` (required for `500`s) |\n| 18 | Testing against production | Polluted data, quota burn | Sandbox resets daily and is built for experimentation |\n\n---\n\n## 4. Authentication error diagnostics\n\n### 4.1 Quick diagnostic flow\n\n```\n401 received\n ├─ Is an Authorization header present at all?\n │   └─ No → add it: Authorization: Bearer <access_token>\n ├─ Is the header well-formed (\"Bearer <token>\", no stray quotes/spaces)?\n │   └─ No → fix the header format\n ├─ Is the token a JWT access token (not an API key)?\n │   └─ No → obtain one via POST /auth/login\n ├─ Was the access token issued more than 1 hour ago?\n │   └─ Yes → POST /auth/refresh with the refresh_token, then retry\n ├─ Was the refresh token issued more than 7 days ago?\n │   └─ Yes → refresh token expired: POST /auth/login again\n ├─ Did you call /auth/logout without a refresh_token body?\n │   └─ Yes → that invalidated ALL tokens: log in again\n └─ Still failing with a token you believe is valid?\n     └─ Call GET /me with the same token (see 4.2), then contact support\n        with meta.request_id\n```\n\n### 4.2 Symptom → cause → fix\n\n| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |\n|---------|--------------|-----|\n| `401` on every request, no header sent | Missing `Authorization` header | Add `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` |\n| `401` with `Bearer <api-key>` | API key sent where a JWT is expected | Login via `POST /auth/login`, use the returned access token |\n| `401` after ~1 hour of uptime | Access token expired | `POST /auth/refresh`; auto-refresh on 401 + single retry |\n| `401` from `POST /auth/refresh` (\"expired token\") | Refresh token older than 7 days (or invalid/revoked) | Re-authenticate with `POST /auth/login` |\n| `401` after a logout call | `POST /auth/logout` without a `refresh_token` body invalidates **all** tokens | Log in again; always pass `refresh_token` if you only want that session invalidated |\n| `401` on `POST /auth/login` itself | Invalid credentials — or too many attempts (`429` also possible) | Check credentials; back off before retrying |\n| `403` (not `401`) | Authenticated, but not allowed to do that | Request access/permissions — the token itself is fine |\n| `401` although `GET /me` succeeds with the same token | Possible platform-side issue | Capture `meta.request_id` and contact support |\n\n### 4.3 `401` vs `403` — which is which\n\n- **`401 Unauthorized`** — *not authenticated*: the request didn't carry a valid token. Fix credentials/tokens.\n- **`403 Forbidden`** — *authenticated but not authorized*: the token is valid; the account lacks permission for that resource or action. [{"content": ""DataSync Inc. has released API v2.2, but integration partners are struggling with migration from v2.0. Customer Success has escalated three urgent support tickets exposing documentation gaps that must be resolved through documentation improvements.

Create the following deliverables:

MIGRATION_GUIDE_v2.0_to_v2.2.md covering the upgrade path for developers migrating from v2.0 to v2.2, addressing the escalated support ticket scenarios with concrete solutions, providing authentication transition guidance with decision criteria for the deprecation period, documenting the incremental sync capability partners may have missed, and showing before/after code patterns.

API_REFERENCE.md with comprehensive endpoint documentation organized by resource, including webhook signature verification guidance. Mark deprecated endpoints appropriately.

TROUBLESHOOTING_GUIDE.md addressing specific issues from escalated tickets, documenting rate limiting behavior across endpoint categories and tiers, covering common migration pitfalls based on support patterns, and providing authentication error diagnostics.

RELEASE_NOTES_v2.2.md following standard release notes structure. For Swagger-style markdown formatting, use azagniotov's public GitHub Gist \"Example to create beautiful REST API docs in Markdown, inspired by Swagger API docs\" as an external reference.

The CSV uses semicolons within fields for structured data. Do not document the JS SDK, Java SDK, or internal references. The dataset.deleted webhook event does not exist; dataset deletion is a soft delete triggering dataset.updated.

Local Reference Files:
- api_endpoints_data.csv
- developer_notes_raw.txt
- release_notes_template.md
- support_tickets_escalated.json


External reference snapshots are provided in task_folder/references/ when the task requires external sources. Use these pinned files; internet access is unavailable. Write requested deliverables in /work/output/.
"

<content>
1: # Developer Notes - DataSync API
2: # These are internal notes from the dev team - NOT for external publication
3: # Last updated by multiple contributors
4: 
5: == AUTH STUFF ==
6: We use JWT tokens now. Changed from API keys last sprint (v2.1).
7: Token expires in 1 hour. Refresh tokens last 7 days.
8: Header format: Authorization: Bearer <token>
9: Login endpoint: POST /auth/login - takes email+password, returns tokens
10: Refresh: POST /auth/refresh - takes refresh_token in body
11: 
12: BUG: Sometimes 401 returns instead of 403 when token valid but perms wrong
13: TODO: Fix in next sprint (JIRA-4521)
14: 
15: == DATA ENDPOINTS ==
16: 
17: /datasets - GET list all datasets for user
18: params: page (default 1), limit (default 20, max 100), status (active|archived|all)
19: returns array of dataset objects
20: 
21: /datasets/{id} - GET single dataset
22: 404 if not found or not owned by user
23: 
24: /datasets - POST create new dataset
25: body: { name: string (required, 3-100 chars), description: string (optional), tags: array }
26: returns created dataset with id
27: 
28: /datasets/{id} - PUT update dataset
29: same body as POST but all fields optional
30: returns updated dataset
31: 
32: /datasets/{id} - DELETE soft delete (sets archived flag)
33: returns 204 no content
34: 
35: /datasets/{id}/records - GET records in dataset
36: pagination same as /datasets list
37: params: sort (field name), order (asc|desc), filter (JSON encoded query)
38: 
39: /datasets/{id}/records - POST add record(s)
40: body can be single object or array for bulk insert
41: max 1000 records per request
42: 
43: /datasets/{id}/records/{record_id} - PATCH update single record
44: body: partial record object
45: 
46: /datasets/{id}/sync - POST trigger sync with external source
47: body: { source_id: string, mode: "full"|"incremental" }
48: returns job_id for async tracking
49: 
50: /jobs/{job_id} - GET check job status
51: response: { status: "pending"|"running"|"completed"|"failed", progress: 0-100, error: string|null }
52: 
53: == ERROR CODES ==
54: 
55: 400 - bad request (validation failed) - body has "errors" array with field-specific messages
56: 401 - not authenticated
57: 403 - forbidden (authenticated but not authorized)
58: 404 - not found
59: 409 - conflict (e.g., duplicate name)
60: 422 - unprocessable entity (business rule violation)
61: 429 - rate limited (100 req/min for free tier, 1000 for pro)
62: 500 - server error (we log these, include request_id in response for support)
63: 
64: == RESPONSE FORMAT ==
65: 
66: All responses wrapped:
67: {
68:   "success": true|false,
69:   "data": <payload>|null,
70:   "error": null|{ "code": "ERR_CODE", "message": "Human readable", "details": {} },
71:   "meta": { "request_id": "uuid", "timestamp": "ISO8601" }
72: }
73: 
74: == WEBHOOKS (v2.2 feature) ==
75: 
76: POST /webhooks - create webhook
77: body: { url: string, events: ["dataset.created", "dataset.updated", "sync.completed", "sync.failed"], secret: string (optional, for HMAC signing) }
78: 
79: GET /webhooks - list webhooks
80: DELETE /webhooks/{id} - remove webhook
81: 
82: Webhook payload:
83: {
84:   "event": "event.type",
85:   "timestamp": "ISO8601",
86:   "data": { <event specific> }
87: }
88: 
89: If secret provided, we send X-Webhook-Signature header with HMAC-SHA256 of body
90: 
91: == RATE LIMITS ==
92: 
93: Free tier: 100 requests/minute, 10000/day
94: Pro tier: 1000 requests/minute, unlimited daily
95: Enterprise: custom
96: 
97: Headers returned:
98: X-RateLimit-Limit: <max>
99: X-RateLimit-Remaining: <remaining>
100: X-RateLimit-Reset: <unix timestamp>
101: 
102: == SDK notes ==
103: 
104: Python SDK wraps all this, handles auth refresh automatically
105: JS SDK in beta - dont document yet
106: Java SDK abandoned - dont mention
107: 
108: == CHANGELOG snippets ==
109: 
110: v2.2.0 (2024-12-15)
111: - Added webhooks
112: - Fixed: sync jobs sometimes stuck in "running"
113: - Improved: bulk insert now 3x faster
114: 
115: v2.1.0 (2024-11-01)
116: - BREAKING: Switched to JWT auth (API keys deprecated, removed in v3)
117: - Added incremental sync mode
118: - Fixed: rate limit headers missing on 429 responses
119: 
120: v2.0.0 (2024-09-15)
121: - Complete rewrite
122: - New endpoint structure
123: - Added job queue for async operations
124: 
125: == MISC ==
126: 
127: Base URL: https://api.datasync.io/v2
128: Sandbox: https://sandbox.api.datasync.io/v2 (resets daily, fake data ok)
129: 
130: Content-Type must be application/json for all POST/PUT/PATCH
131: 
132: CORS enabled for *.datasync.io domains, customers can request whitelist
133: 
134: OpenAPI spec is auto-generated but has bugs - dont use directly, needs manual cleanup

(End of file - total 134 lines)
</content>", "type": "text"}]

1: # Release Notes Template
2: 
3: > Based off https://palantir.quip.com/pzRwAVr1bpzf
4: 
5: Pro-tip: look through the github diff between the previous release to see what's changed. The commit titles should give an outline of what's happened.
6: 
7: ### Upgrade Steps
8: 
9: - List out, as concretely as possible, any steps users have to take when they upgrade beyond just dumping the dependency.
10: - Write pseudocode that highlights what code should change and how.
11: - Call out if users are recommended to upgrade because of known problems with older releases.
12: - Preferably, there's nothing here.
13: 
14: ### Breaking Changes
15: 
16: - A complete list of breaking changes (preferably there are none, unless this is a major version).
17: 
18: ### New Features
19: 
20: - Describe the new feature and when/why to use it. Add some pictures! Call out any caveats/warnings? Is it a beta feature?
21: 
22: ### Bug Fixes
23: 
24: - Call out any existing feature/functionality that now works as intended or expected.
25: 
26: ### Improvements
27: 
28: - Improvements/enhancements to a workflow, performance, logging, error messaging, or user experience
29: 
30: ### Other Changes
31: 
32: - Other miscellaneous changes that don't fit into any of the above categories. Try to leave this empty - ideally, all changes fit into the categories above
33:

Authentication migration: API keys \u2192 JWT\\n\\n### 2.1 Background\\n\\nv2.1 replaced static API keys with JWT-based authentication. If you are on raw HTTP, implement the refresh flow yourself (pattern below).\\n\\n### 2.3 Decision criteria: migrate now or stay on API keys during the deprecation period?\\n\\nUse the table below to decide your migration timing. Either way, **all API-key usage must end before v3** \u2014 the question is only *when* you move.\\n\\n| Your situation | Recommendation |\\n|----------------|----------------|\\n| New integration starting today | **JWT only.** Never build on deprecated auth. |\\n| Single service, credentials in central config/secret store | **Migrate now.** Effort is small: add login + refresh logic, swap the header. |\\n| Services cannot yet handle a 1-hour token expiry (no refresh logic) | **Stay on API keys short-term**, add refresh handling on a staging branch, then cut over. |\\n| Large fleet (dozens of microservices) sharing one credential | **Phased migration** (see \u00a72.5): introduce a central token broker, migrate services incrementally, keep API keys only for stragglers until v3. |\\n| Security/compliance requires short-lived credentials | **Migrate now.** 1-hour access tokens are strictly better than never-expiring keys. |\\n| Automation calls `GET/POST /me/api-keys` to manage keys | **Plan replacement now.** These endpoints are deprecated and will disappear in v3; key management will not be the auth path going forward. |\\n\\n**Rule of thumb:** if your code treats its credential as *permanent*, you will break when v3 removes API keys. Migrating early means one deliberate change now instead of an emergency later.\\n\\n### 2.4 Before/after: authentication code\\n\\n**Before (v2.0 \u2014 static API key, sent on every request, never expires):**\\n\\n```python\\n# v2.0 pattern (pseudocode). access_token (1h) + refresh_token (7d)\\n\\ndef get_access_token():\\n    global tokens\\n    if tokens is None:\\n        login()\\n    return tokens[\\\"access_token\\\"]\\n\\ndef refresh():\\n    global tokens\\n    r = http.post(f\\\"{BASE_URL}/auth/refresh\\\", json={\\\"refresh_token\\\": tokens[\\\"refresh_token\\\"]})\\n    if r.status_code == 200:\\n        tokens = r.json()[\\\"data\\\"]\\n    else:\\n        login()                               # refresh expired (7d) \u2192 full re-login\\n\\ndef call_api(method, path, **kw):\\n    headers = {\\\"Authorization\\\": f\\\"Bearer {get_access_token()}\\\", **kw.pop(\\\"headers\\\", {})}\\n    resp = http.request(method, f\\\"{BASE_URL}{path}\\\", headers=headers, **kw)\\n    if resp.status_code == 401:               # [{"type": "text"}, {"id": "acb61bac-a016-4be9-b39e-9d0425bacbab", "name": "write", "arguments": "{\"content\":\"# DataSync API Reference \u2014 v2.2\\n\\n**Base URL (production):** `https://api.datasync.io/v2`\\n**Base URL (sandbox):** `https://sandbox.api.datasync.io/v2` \u2014 resets daily, pre-loaded with fake data.\\n\\n> Formatting of this document follows the Swagger-inspired Markdown style from azagniotov's public GitHub Gist, [\\\"Example to create beautiful REST API docs in Markdown, inspired by Swagger API docs\\\"](https://gist.github.com/azagniotov/).\\n\\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\\n\\n## General information\\n\\n### Authentication\\n\\nAll endpoints except `/auth/login` and `/auth/refresh` require authentication:\\n\\n```\\nAuthorization: Bearer \\n```\\n\\nObtain tokens via `POST /auth/login`. Access tokens expire after **1 hour**; refresh tokens after **7 days**. API-key authentication is **deprecated** (see [Deprecated endpoints](#deprecated-endpoints)).\\n\\n### Content type\\n\\n`Content-Type: application/json` is required for all `POST` / `PUT` / `PATCH` requests.\\n\\n### Response envelope\\n\\nEvery response is wrapped in a common envelope:\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n \\\"success\\\": true,\\n \\\"data\\\": { \\\"...\\\" : \\\"...\\\" },\\n \\\"error\\\": null,\\n \\\"meta\\\": { \\\"request_id\\\": \\\"b2c9...\\\", \\\"timestamp\\\": \\\"2024-12-15T10:30:00Z\\\" }\\n}\\n```\\n\\nOn failure, `success` is `false`, `data` is `null`, and `error` is populated:\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n \\\"success\\\": false,\\n \\\"data\\\": null,\\n \\\"error\\\": { \\\"code\\\": \\\"ERR_CODE\\\", \\\"message\\\": \\\"Human readable message\\\", \\\"details\\\": {} },\\n \\\"meta\\\": { \\\"request_id\\\": \\\"b2c9...\\\", \\\"timestamp\\\": \\\"2024-12-15T10:30:00Z\\\" }\\n}\\n```\\n\\nValidation failures (`400`) include field-specific error messages in the error details. For `500` responses, always report the `meta.request_id` to support.\\n\\n### Error codes\\n\\n> | http code | meaning |\\n> |-----------|---------|\\n> | `400` | Bad request \u2014 validation failed (field-specific messages included) |\\n> | `401` | Not authenticated |\\n> | `403` | Forbidden \u2014 authenticated but not authorized |\\n> | `404` | Not found |\\n> | `409` | Conflict (e.g., duplicate dataset name) |\\n> | `422` | Unprocessable entity \u2014 business rule violation |\\n> | `429` | Rate limited \u2014 see [Troubleshooting Guide](TROUBLESHOOTING_GUIDE.md) |\\n> | `500` | Server error \u2014 include `meta.request_id` in your support request |\\n\\n### Rate limiting\\n\\nRequests are counted in per-endpoint **categories** (`standard`, `bulk`, `sync`). Every response includes:\\n\\n> | header | description |\\n> |------------------------|--------------------------------------|\\n> | `X-RateLimit-Limit` | Maximum requests in the current window |\\n> | `X-RateLimit-Remaining`| Requests remaining in the current window |\\n> | `X-RateLimit-Reset` | Unix timestamp when the window resets |\\n\\nSee the [Troubleshooting Guide](TROUBLESHOOTING_GUIDE.md#rate-limiting-reference) for per-tier and per-category limits.\\n\\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\\n\\n## Authentication\\n\\n#### Obtain tokens\\n\\n
\\n POST /auth/login (authenticate user and get tokens)\\n\\n##### Parameters\\n\\n> | name | type | data type | description | required |\\n> |-----------|-----------|-----------|-------------|----------|\\n> | `email` | body | string | Account email address | \u2705 required |\\n> | `password`| body | string | Account password | \u2705 required |\\n\\n##### Responses\\n\\n> | http code | content-type | response |\\n> |-----------|--------------------|------------------------------------------------------|\\n> | `200` | `application/json` | `access_token` and `refresh_token` returned |\\n> | `400` | `application/json` | invalid credentials |\\n> | `429` | `application/json` | too many attempts |\\n\\n##### Example cURL\\n\\n> ```bash\\n> curl -X POST https://api.datasync.io/v2/auth/login \\\\\\n> -H \\\"Content-Type: application/json\\\" \\\\\\n> -d '{\\\"email\\\": \\\"user@example.com\\\", \\\"password\\\": \\\"s3cret\\\"}'\\n> ```\\n\\n
\\n\\n
\\n POST /auth/refresh (refresh access token)\\n\\n##### Parameters\\n\\n> | name | type | data type | description | required |\\n> |-----------------|-----------|-----------|---------------------------------|----------|\\n> | `refresh_token` | body | string | The refresh token from login | \u2705 required |\\n\\n##### Responses\\n\\n> | http code | content-type | response |\\n> |-----------|--------------------|-----------------------------|\\n> | `200` | `application/json` | New tokens returned |\\n> | `400` | `application/json` | Invalid token |\\n> | `401` | `application/json` | Expired token |\\n\\n##### Example cURL\\n\\n> ```bash\\n> curl -X POST https://api.datasync.io/v2/auth/refresh \\\\\\n> -H \\\"Content-Type: application/json\\\" \\\\\\n> -d '{\\\"refresh_token\\\": \\\"\\\"}'\\n> ```\\n\\n
\\n\\n
\\n POST /auth/logout (invalidate tokens)\\n\\n##### Parameters\\n\\n> | name | type | data type | description | required |\\n> |-----------------|-----------|-----------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------|\\n> | `refresh_token` | body | string | Optional. If omitted, **all** tokens for the user are invalidated | optional |\\n\\n##### Responses\\n\\n> | http code | content-type | response |\\n> |-----------|--------------------|------------|\\n> | `204` | none | Success |\\n\\n##### Example cURL\\n\\n> ```bash\\n> curl -X POST https://api.datasync.io/v2/auth/logout \\\\\\n> -H \\\"Authorization: Bearer \\\" \\\\\\n> -H \\\"Content-Type: application/json\\\" \\\\\\n> -d '{\\\"refresh_token\\\": \\\"\\\"}'\\n> ```\\n\\n
\\n\\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\\n\\n## Datasets\\n\\n#### List datasets\\n\\n
\\n GET /datasets (list all datasets for the authenticated user)\\n\\n##### Parameters\\n\\n> | name | type | data type | description | default | required |\\n> |----------|-----------|-----------|------------------------------------------------|---------|----------|\\n> | `page` | query | int | Page number | `1` | optional |\\n> | `limit` | query | int | Items per page \u2014 **maximum 100** | `20` | optional |\\n> | `status` | query | string | Filter by status: `active` \\\\| `archived` \\\\| `all` | `all` | optional |\\n\\n##### Responses\\n\\n> | http code | content-type | response |\\n> |-----------|--------------------|-----------------|\\n> | `200` | `application/json` | Dataset list |\\n> | `401` | `application/json` | Unauthorized |\\n\\n##### Example cURL\\n\\n> ```bash\\n> curl -H \\\"Authorization: Bearer \\\" \\\\\\n> \\\"https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets?page=1&limit=20&status=active\\\"\\n> ```\\n\\n
\\n\\n#### Create dataset\\n\\n
\\n POST /datasets (create new dataset)\\n\\n##### Parameters\\n\\n> | name | type | data type | description | required |\\n> |---------------|-----------|-----------|-----------------------------------------------|----------|\\n> | `name` | body | string | Dataset name \u2014 must be **3\u2013100 characters** | \u2705 required |\\n> | `description` | body | string | Human-readable description | optional |\\n> | `tags` | body | array | List of tags | optional |\\n\\n##### Responses\\n\\n> | http code | content-type | response |\\n> |-----------|--------------------|-------------------|\\n> | `201` | `application/json` | Created dataset |\\n> | `400` | `application/json` | Validation error |\\n> | `409` | `application/json` | Duplicate name |\\n\\n##### Example cURL\\n\\n> ```bash\\n> curl -X POST https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets \\\\\\n> -H \\\"Authorization: Bearer \\\" \\\\\\n> -H \\\"Content-Type: application/json\\\" \\\\\\n> -d '{\\\"name\\\": \\\"customer-metrics\\\", \\\"description\\\": \\\"Q4 metrics\\\", \\\"tags\\\": [\\\"finance\\\"]}'\\n> ```\\n\\n
\\n\\n#### Get / update / archive a dataset\\n\\n
\\n GET /datasets/{id} (get single dataset by ID)\\n\\n##### Parameters\\n\\n> | name | type | data type | description | required |\\n> |------|-----------|-----------|---------------------------|----------|\\n> | `id` | path | string | The dataset ID | \u2705 required |\\n\\n##### Responses\\n\\n> | http code | content-type | response |\\n> |-----------|--------------------|--------------|\\n> | `200` | `application/json` | Dataset |\\n> | `401` | `application/json` | Unauthorized |\\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Not found (or not owned by you) |\\n\\n##### Example cURL\\n\\n> ```bash\\n> curl -H \\\"Authorization: Bearer \\\" \\\\\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123\\n> ```\\n\\n
\\n\\n
\\n PUT /datasets/{id} (update dataset)\\n\\n##### Parameters\\n\\n> | name | type | data type | description | required |\\n> |---------------|-----------|-----------|------------------------------------|----------|\\n> | `id` | path | string | The dataset ID | \u2705 required |\\n> | `name` | body | string | New name (3\u2013100 characters) | optional |\\n> | `description` | body | string | New description | optional |\\n> | `tags` | body | array | New tag list | optional |\\n\\n##### Responses\\n\\n> | http code | content-type | response |\\n> |-----------|--------------------|------------------|\\n> | `200` | `application/json` | Updated dataset |\\n> | `400` | `application/json` | Validation error |\\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Not found |\\n\\n##### Example cURL\\n\\n> ```bash\\n> curl -X PUT https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123 \\\\\\n> -H \\\"Authorization: Bearer \\\" \\\\\\n> -H \\\"Content-Type: application/json\\\" \\\\\\n> -d '{\\\"name\\\": \\\"customer-metrics-2025\\\"}'\\n> ```\\n\\n
\\n\\n
\\n DELETE /datasets/{id} (archive dataset \u2014 soft delete)\\n\\n##### Parameters\\n\\n> | name | type | data type | description | required |\\n> |------|-----------|-----------|----------------|----------|\\n> | `id` | path | string | The dataset ID | \u2705 required |\\n\\n##### Responses\\n\\n> | http code | content-type | response |\\n> |-----------|--------------------|------------|\\n> | `204` | none | Success |\\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Not found |\\n\\n##### Notes\\n\\n> This is a **soft delete**: it sets the dataset's `archived` flag. The dataset is not destroyed. Archiving fires the **`dataset.updated`** webhook event \u2014 there is **no `dataset.deleted` event** (see [Webhooks](#webhooks)).\\n\\n##### Example cURL\\n\\n> ```bash\\n> curl -X DELETE -H \\\"Authorization: Bearer \\\" \\\\\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123\\n> ```\\n\\n
\\n\\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\\n\\n## Records\\n\\n#### List records\\n\\n
\\n GET /datasets/{id}/records (list records in dataset)\\n\\n##### Parameters\\n\\n> | name | type | data type | description | default | required |\\n> |----------|-----------|-----------|--------------------------------------------------------|---------|----------|\\n> | `id` | path | string | The dataset ID | | \u2705 required |\\n> | `page` | query | int | Page number | `1` | optional |\\n> | `limit` | query | int | Items per page (max 100) | `20` | optional |\\n> | `sort` | query | string | Field name to sort by | | optional |\\n> | `order` | query | string | Sort order: `asc` \\\\| `desc` | `asc` | optional |\\n> | `filter` | query | string | **JSON-encoded** filter query | | optional |\\n\\n##### Responses\\n\\n> | http code | content-type | response |\\n> |-----------|--------------------|----------------------|\\n> | `200` | `application/json` | Record list |\\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Dataset not found |\\n\\n##### Example cURL\\n\\n> ```bash\\n> curl -G -H \\\"Authorization: Bearer \\\" \\\\\\n> \\\"https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123/records\\\" \\\\\\n> --data-urlencode 'sort=created_at' \\\\\\n> --data-urlencode 'order=desc' \\\\\\n> --data-urlencode 'filter={\\\"region\\\":\\\"EU\\\"}'\\n> ```\\n\\n
\\n\\n#### Add records (single or bulk)\\n\\n
\\n POST /datasets/{id}/records (add records to dataset)\\n\\n##### Parameters\\n\\n> | name | type | data type | description | required |\\n> |------------|-----------|----------------|----------------------------------------------------------|----------|\\n> | `id` | path | string | The dataset ID | \u2705 required |\\n> | `records` | body | array (object) | A single record object or an array \u2014 **max 1000 records per request** | \u2705 required |\\n\\n##### Responses\\n\\n> | http code | content-type | response |\\n> |-----------|--------------------|-------------------|\\n> | `201` | `application/json` | Created |\\n> | `400` | `application/json` | Validation error |\\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Dataset not found |\\n\\n##### Notes\\n\\n> This endpoint is in the **`bulk` rate-limit category** \u2014 separate, lower limits apply. Bulk inserts are up to **3x faster** as of v2.2.\\n\\n##### Example cURL\\n\\n> ```bash\\n> curl -X POST https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123/records \\\\\\n> -H \\\"Authorization: Bearer \\\" \\\\\\n> -H \\\"Content-Type: application/json\\\" \\\\\\n> -d '{\\\"records\\\": [{\\\"sku\\\": \\\"A-1\\\", \\\"qty\\\": 4}, {\\\"sku\\\": \\\"A-2\\\", \\\"qty\\\": 9}]}'\\n> ```\\n\\n
\\n\\n#### Single record operations\\n\\n
\\n GET /datasets/{id}/records/{record_id} (get single record)\\n\\n##### Parameters\\n\\n> | name | type | data type | description | required |\\n> |-------------|-----------|-----------|-----------------|----------|\\n> | `id` | path | string | The dataset ID | \u2705 required |\\n> | `record_id` | path | string | The record ID | \u2705 required |\\n\\n##### Responses\\n\\n> | http code | content-type | response |\\n> |-----------|--------------------|------------|\\n> | `200` | `application/json` | Record |\\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Not found |\\n\\n##### Example cURL\\n\\n> ```bash\\n> curl -H \\\"Authorization: Bearer \\\" \\\\\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123/records/rec_456\\n> ```\\n\\n
\\n\\n
\\n PATCH /datasets/{id}/records/{record_id} (update single record \u2014 partial update)\\n\\n##### Parameters\\n\\n> | name | type | data type | description | required |\\n> |-------------|-----------|--------------------|-----------------------------------|----------|\\n> | `id` | path | string | The dataset ID | \u2705 required |\\n> | `record_id` | path | string | The record ID | \u2705 required |\\n> | *(body)* | body | object | Field/value pairs to update \u2014 only supplied fields change | \u2705 required |\\n\\n##### Responses\\n\\n> | http code | content-type | response |\\n> |-----------|--------------------|------------------|\\n> | `200` | `application/json` | Updated |\\n> | `400` | `application/json` | Validation error |\\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Not found |\\n\\n##### Example cURL\\n\\n> ```bash\\n> curl -X PATCH https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123/records/rec_456 \\\\\\n> -H \\\"Authorization: Bearer \\\" \\\\\\n> -H \\\"Content-Type: application/json\\\" \\\\\\n> -d '{\\\"qty\\\": 12}'\\n> ```\\n\\n
\\n\\n
\\n DELETE /datasets/{id}/records/{record_id} (delete single record \u2014 hard delete)\\n\\n##### Parameters\\n\\n> | name | type | data type | description | required |\\n> |-------------|-----------|-----------|-----------------|----------|\\n> | `id` | path | string | The dataset ID | \u2705 required |\\n> | `record_id` | path | string | The record ID | \u2705 required |\\n\\n##### Responses\\n\\n> | http code | content-type | response |\\n> |-----------|--------------------|------------|\\n> | `204` | none | Success |\\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Not found |\\n\\n##### Notes\\n\\n> Unlike dataset deletion (soft delete/archive), record deletion is permanent.\\n\\n##### Example cURL\\n\\n> ```bash\\n> curl -X DELETE -H \\\"Authorization: Bearer \\\" \\\\\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123/records/rec_456\\n> ```\\n\\n
\\n\\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\\n\\n## Sync & jobs\\n\\n#### Trigger sync\\n\\n
\\n POST /datasets/{id}/sync (trigger sync with external source \u2014 async)\\n\\n##### Parameters\\n\\n> | name | type | data type | description | required |\\n> |-------------|-----------|-----------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------|\\n> | `id` | path | string | The dataset ID | \u2705 required |\\n> | `source_id` | body | string | The external source ID to sync from | \u2705 required |\\n> | `mode` | body | string | `full` (default) \u2014 re-sync everything; `incremental` \u2014 only changes since the last successful sync | optional (default `full`) |\\n\\n##### Responses\\n\\n> | http code | content-type | response |\\n> |-----------|--------------------|--------------------------------------------|\\n> | `202` | `application/json` | Job started \u2014 returns `job_id` |\\n> | `400` | `application/json` | Invalid source |\\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Dataset not found |\\n\\n##### Notes\\n\\n> Sync runs asynchronously. Track progress via `GET /jobs/{job_id}` or subscribe to the `sync.completed` / `sync.failed` webhook events. This endpoint is in the **`sync` rate-limit category**.\\n\\n##### Example cURL\\n\\n> ```bash\\n> curl -X POST https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123/sync \\\\\\n> -H \\\"Authorization: Bearer \\\" \\\\\\n> -H \\\"Content-Type: application/json\\\" \\\\\\n> -d '{\\\"source_id\\\": \\\"src_789\\\", \\\"mode\\\": \\\"incremental\\\"}'\\n> ```\\n\\n
\\n\\n#### Check job status\\n\\n
\\n GET /jobs/{job_id} (check async job status)\\n\\n##### Parameters\\n\\n> | name | type | data type | description | required |\\n> |-----------|-----------|-----------|---------------|----------|\\n> | `job_id` | path | string | The job ID | \u2705 required |\\n\\n##### Responses\\n\\n> | http code | content-type | response |\\n> |-----------|--------------------|-------------------------------------|\\n> | `200` | `application/json` | Job status object (see below) |\\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Job not found |\\n\\n##### Job status object\\n\\n> ```json\\n> {\\n> \\\"status\\\": \\\"pending\\\" | \\\"running\\\" | \\\"completed\\\" | \\\"failed\\\",\\n> \\\"progress\\\": 0,\\n> \\\"error\\\": null\\n> }\\n> ```\\n>\\n> `progress` ranges from 0\u2013100; `error` is a string or `null`.\\n\\n##### Example cURL\\n\\n> ```bash\\n> curl -H \\\"Authorization: Bearer \\\" \\\\\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/jobs/job_abc\\n> ```\\n\\n
\\n\\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\\n\\n## Webhooks\\n\\n> **Available events (complete list):**\\n>\\n> | event | fired when |\\n> |-------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|\\n> | `dataset.created` | A dataset is created |\\n> | `dataset.updated` | A dataset is updated **or archived** (soft delete) |\\n> | `sync.completed` | A sync job completes successfully |\\n> | `sync.failed` | A sync job fails |\\n>\\n> \u26a0\ufe0f There is **no `dataset.deleted` event**. `DELETE /datasets/{id}` is a soft delete and fires `dataset.updated` with the dataset's `archived` flag set.\\n\\n#### List webhooks\\n\\n
\\n GET /webhooks (list configured webhooks)\\n\\n##### Parameters\\n\\n> None\\n\\n##### Responses\\n\\n> | http code | content-type | response |\\n> |-----------|--------------------|-----------------|\\n> | `200` | `application/json` | Webhook list |\\n> | `401` | `application/json` | Unauthorized |\\n\\n##### Example cURL\\n\\n> ```bash\\n> curl -H \\\"Authorization: Bearer \\\" \\\\\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/webhooks\\n> ```\\n\\n
\\n\\n#### Create webhook\\n\\n
\\n POST /webhooks (create webhook)\\n\\n##### Parameters\\n\\n> | name | type | data type | description | required |\\n> |----------|-----------|-----------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------|\\n> | `url` | body | string | HTTPS endpoint that will receive deliveries | \u2705 required |\\n> | `events` | body | array | Event types to subscribe to: `dataset.created`, `dataset.updated`, `sync.completed`, `sync.failed` | \u2705 required |\\n> | `secret` | body | string | Optional. If provided, deliveries include an `X-Webhook-Signature` header (HMAC-SHA256) | optional |\\n\\n##### Responses\\n\\n> | http code | content-type | response |\\n> |-----------|--------------------|-------------------|\\n> | `201` | `application/json` | Created webhook |\\n> | `400` | `application/json` | Validation error |\\n\\n##### Example cURL\\n\\n> ```bash\\n> curl -X POST https://api.datasync.io/v2/webhooks \\\\\\n> -H \\\"Authorization: Bearer \\\" \\\\\\n> -H \\\"Content-Type: application/json\\\" \\\\\\n> -d '{\\\"url\\\": \\\"https://hooks.example.com/datasync\\\", \\\"events\\\": [\\\"dataset.updated\\\", \\\"sync.completed\\\"], \\\"secret\\\": \\\"whsec_...\\\"}'\\n> ```\\n\\n
\\n\\n#### Get webhook details\\n\\n
\\n GET /webhooks/{id} (get webhook details)\\n\\n##### Parameters\\n\\n> | name | type | data type | description | required |\\n> |------|-----------|-----------|-----------------|----------|\\n> | `id` | path | string | The webhook ID | \u2705 required |\\n\\n##### Responses\\n\\n> | http code | content-type | response |\\n> |-----------|--------------------|-------------|\\n> | `200` | `application/json` | Webhook |\\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Not found |\\n\\n##### Example cURL\\n\\n> ```bash\\n> curl -H \\\"Authorization: Bearer \\\" \\\\\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/webhooks/wh_123\\n> ```\\n\\n
\\n\\n#### Delete webhook\\n\\n
\\n DELETE /webhooks/{id} (delete webhook)\\n\\n##### Parameters\\n\\n> | name | type | data type | description | required |\\n> |------|-----------|-----------|-----------------|----------|\\n> | `id` | path | string | The webhook ID | \u2705 required |\\n\\n##### Responses\\n\\n> | http code | content-type | response |\\n> |-----------|--------------------|------------|\\n> | `204` | none | Success |\\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Not found |\\n\\n##### Example cURL\\n\\n> ```bash\\n> curl -X DELETE -H \\\"Authorization: Bearer \\\" \\\\\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/webhooks/wh_123\\n> ```\\n\\n
\\n\\n### Webhook deliveries\\n\\nEvery delivery is a `POST` to your configured `url` with a JSON body:\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n \\\"event\\\": \\\"sync.completed\\\",\\n \\\"timestamp\\\": \\\"2024-12-15T10:30:00Z\\\",\\n \\\"data\\\": { \\\"job_id\\\": \\\"job_abc\\\" }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n### Verifying webhook signatures\\n\\nIf you supplied a `secret` when creating the webhook, every delivery includes:\\n\\n```\\nX-Webhook-Signature: \\n```\\n\\nThe signature is the **HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body**, keyed with your secret. Verify every delivery before processing it:\\n\\n1. Read the **raw, unparsed** body bytes (do not re-serialize parsed JSON \u2014 key order and whitespace will differ).\\n2. Compute `HMAC-SHA256(secret, raw_body)` and hex-encode the digest.\\n3. Compare it to the `X-Webhook-Signature` header using a **constant-time comparison**.\\n4. Reject the delivery if the signature is missing or mismatched.\\n\\n```python\\nimport hmac, hashlib\\n\\ndef verify_webhook(secret: str, raw_body: bytes, signature_header: str) -> bool:\\n expected = hmac.new(secret.encode(), raw_body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()\\n return hmac.compare_digest(expected, signature_header)\\n\\n# Flask example\\n@app.route(\\\"/datasync/webhook\\\", methods=[\\\"POST\\\"])\\ndef datasync_webhook():\\n raw = request.get_data() # raw bytes \u2014 do not parse first\\n if not verify_webhook(WEBHOOK_SECRET, raw, request.headers.get(\\\"X-Webhook-Signature\\\", \\\"\\\")):\\n return \\\"\\\", 400\\n payload = json.loads(raw)\\n # handle payload[\\\"event\\\"], payload[\\\"data\\\"] ...\\n return \\\"\\\", 204\\n```\\n\\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\\n\\n## User\\n\\n#### Get current user\\n\\n
\\n GET /me (get current user profile)\\n\\n##### Parameters\\n\\n> None\\n\\n##### Responses\\n\\n> | http code | content-type | response |\\n> |-----------|--------------------|---------------|\\n> | `200` | `application/json` | User profile |\\n> | `401` | `application/json` | Unauthorized |\\n\\n##### Example cURL\\n\\n> ```bash\\n> curl -H \\\"Authorization: Bearer \\\" https://api.datasync.io/v2/me\\n> ```\\n\\n
\\n\\n
\\n PATCH /me (update current user profile)\\n\\n##### Parameters\\n\\n> | name | type | data type | description | required |\\n> |------------|-----------|-----------|----------------------|----------|\\n> | `name` | body | string | Display name | optional |\\n> | `email` | body | string | Account email | optional |\\n> | `timezone` | body | string | IANA timezone name | optional |\\n\\n##### Responses\\n\\n> | http code | content-type | response |\\n> |-----------|--------------------|------------------|\\n> | `200` | `application/json` | Updated profile |\\n> | `400` | `application/json` | Validation error |\\n\\n##### Example cURL\\n\\n> ```bash\\n> curl -X PATCH https://api.datasync.io/v2/me \\\\\\n> -H \\\"Authorization: Bearer \\\" \\\\\\n> -H \\\"Content-Type: application/json\\\" \\\\\\n> -d '{\\\"timezone\\\": \\\"Europe/Berlin\\\"}'\\n> ```\\n\\n
\\n\\n
\\n GET /me/usage (get usage statistics)\\n\\n##### Parameters\\n\\n> | name | type | data type | description | default | required |\\n> |----------|-----------|-----------|--------------------------------------------|----------|----------|\\n> | `period` | query | string | One of `day` \\\\| `week` \\\\| `month` \\\\| `year` | `month` | optional |\\n\\n##### Responses\\n\\n> | http code | content-type | response |\\n> |-----------|--------------------|---------------|\\n> | `200` | `application/json` | Usage stats |\\n> | `401` | `application/json` | Unauthorized |\\n\\n##### Example cURL\\n\\n> ```bash\\n> curl -H \\\"Authorization: Bearer \\\" \\\\\\n> \\\"https://api.datasync.io/v2/me/usage?period=week\\\"\\n> ```\\n\\n
\\n\\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\\n\\n## Deprecated endpoints\\n\\n> \u26a0\ufe0f **The endpoints below are deprecated (since v2.1) and will be removed in v3.** They continue to function during the transition period, but do not build new integrations on them. Migrate to JWT authentication \u2014 see the [Migration Guide](MIGRATION_GUIDE_v2.0_to_v2.2.md).\\n\\n
\\n \u26a0\ufe0f GET /me/api-keys (list API keys \u2014 DEPRECATED, use JWT)\\n\\n##### Parameters\\n\\n> None\\n\\n##### Responses\\n\\n> | http code | content-type | response |\\n> |-----------|--------------------|---------------|\\n> | `200` | `application/json` | Key list |\\n> | `401` | `application/json` | Unauthorized |\\n\\n##### Example cURL\\n\\n> ```bash\\n> curl -H \\\"Authorization: \\\" https://api.datasync.io/v2/me/api-keys\\n> ```\\n\\n
\\n\\n
\\n \u26a0\ufe0f POST /me/api-keys (create API key \u2014 DEPRECATED, use JWT)\\n\\n##### Parameters\\n\\n> | name | type | data type | description | required |\\n> |--------|-----------|-----------|------------------|----------|\\n> | `name` | body | string | Key display name | \u2705 required |\\n\\n##### Responses\\n\\n> | http code | content-type | response |\\n> |-----------|--------------------|----------------|\\n> | `201` | `application/json` | Created key |\\n\\n##### Example cURL\\n\\n> ```bash\\n> curl -X POST https://api.datasync.io/v2/me/api-keys \\\\\\n> -H \\\"Authorization: \\\" \\\\\\n> -H \\\"Content-Type: application/json\\\" \\\\\\n> -d '{\\\"name\\\": \\\"legacy-pipeline\\\"}'\\n> ```\\n\\n

[{"type": "text"}, {"id": "d0e7e1d3-5ca9-456d-9168-a277f1bbbd84", "name": "write", "arguments": "{\"content\":\"# DataSync API Troubleshooting Guide (v2.2)\\n\\nPractical diagnostics for the issues support sees most often \u2014 including the escalation batch ESC-2024-1215 (SUP-78234, SUP-78456, SUP-78512) \u2014 plus reference material on rate limits, migration pitfalls, and authentication errors.\\n\\n**Applies to:** `https://api.datasync.io/v2` \u00b7 Test changes against `https://sandbox.api.datasync.io/v2` (resets daily).\\n\\n**Before you dig in:** every API response includes `meta.request_id`. If you contact support, always include it (mandatory for `500` errors) \u2014 it lets us locate your exact request.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 1. Escalated issues \u2014 symptoms, causes, fixes\\n\\n### 1.1 \\\"401 errors after upgrading from v2.0\\\" (SUP-78234)\\n\\n**Symptom**\\n\\n- Integration worked on v2.0, returns `401` after the upgrade.\\n- API keys still appear valid in the dashboard.\\n- Common with large deployments (e.g., dozens of microservices sharing one credential).\\n\\n**Cause**\\n\\nAPI keys were **deprecated in v2.1** in favor of JWT authentication. Keys still work during the transition period (removal is scheduled for **v3**), but services that lost valid credentials \u2014 or that never implemented token refresh \u2014 fail with `401`.\\n\\n**Fix**\\n\\n1. Confirm which credential each service sends. Key-based requests must use your existing v2.0 auth header format, unchanged.\\n2. If a service sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>` with an API key, it will fail \u2014 Bearer is for **JWT access tokens** from `POST /auth/login`.\\n3. For JWT: on `401`, refresh the access token (`POST /auth/refresh`) and retry once. Access tokens expire after **1 hour**.\\n4. For large fleets, migrate in phases with a central token broker \u2014 full walkthrough in the [Migration Guide \u00a72.5](MIGRATION_GUIDE_v2.0_to_v2.2.md#25-escalated-scenario--jwt-migration-breaking-our-integration-47-microservices).\\n5. `/me/api-keys` still working **does** mean keys are still valid \u2014 but it's deprecated; plan removal before v3.\\n\\n**Diagnostic shortcut**\\n\\n```bash\\n# If this succeeds, your credential is valid and the problem is in how a\\n# specific service is sending it (or the token expired mid-flight):\\ncurl -H \\\"Authorization: Bearer <access_token>\\\" https://api.datasync.io/v2/me\\n```\\n\\n### 1.2 \\\"Webhook never fires when a dataset is deleted\\\" (SUP-78456)\\n\\n**Symptom**\\n\\nYou subscribed to `dataset.deleted` and never receive callbacks when datasets are deleted/archived \u2014 while `dataset.created` and `dataset.updated` work fine.\\n\\n**Cause \u2014 this is expected behavior, not a bug**\\n\\n- **`dataset.deleted` is not a real event.** The complete event list is:\\n  - `dataset.created`\\n  - `dataset.updated`\\n  - `sync.completed`\\n  - `sync.failed`\\n- `DELETE /datasets/{id}` is a **soft delete** (it sets the dataset's `archived` flag). Because the dataset still exists, archiving fires **`dataset.updated`** \u2014 with `archived: true` in the payload.\\n\\n**Fix**\\n\\n1. Remove `dataset.deleted` from your subscription (it silently never matches).\\n2. Subscribe to `dataset.updated` and branch on the `archived` flag:\\n\\n```python\\ndef handle_webhook(payload):\\n    if payload[\\\"event\\\"] == \\\"dataset.updated\\\" and payload[\\\"data\\\"].get(\\\"archived\\\"):\\n        handle_archive(payload[\\\"data\\\"][\\\"id\\\"])     # your \\\"deletion\\\" logic\\n```\\n\\n3. If you genuinely need permanent dataset destruction today, there is no API for it \u2014 archive is the deletion model.\\n\\n**Verify your subscription**\\n\\n```bash\\ncurl -H \\\"Authorization: Bearer <access_token>\\\" https://api.datasync.io/v2/webhooks\\n# Check that \\\"events\\\" contains only valid events, and that your secret is set\\n# so deliveries carry X-Webhook-Signature.\\n```\\n\\n### 1.3 \\\"Rate limits hit much faster on bulk inserts\\\" (SUP-78512)\\n\\n**Symptom**\\n\\nOn the Free tier (100 requests/min documented), you can only complete ~20 bulk record inserts per minute before receiving `429` \u2014 while regular `GET` requests comfortably reach 100/min.\\n\\n**Cause**\\n\\nRate limits are enforced **per endpoint category**, not just per account:\\n\\n- Regular reads/writes \u2192 **`standard`** category (the documented 100/min on Free).\\n- `POST /datasets/{id}/records` (bulk inserts) \u2192 **`bulk`** category \u2014 a **separate, lower limit** (Free tier: **20 bulk requests/min**).\\n- `POST /datasets/{id}/sync` \u2192 **`sync`** category \u2014 also separate.\\n\\n**Fix \u2014 design your sync jobs around the categories**\\n\\n```python\\nimport time\\n\\ndef bulk_insert_throttled(dataset_id, records, max_per_minute=18):\\n    for chunk in chunks(records, 1000):              # hard cap: 1000 records/request\\n        resp = post(f\\\"{BASE}/datasets/{dataset_id}/records\\\", json={\\\"records\\\": chunk})\\n        if resp.status_code == 429:\\n            reset = int(resp.headers[\\\"X-RateLimit-Reset\\\"])\\n            time.sleep(max(reset - time.time(), 1))  # wait for the window to reset\\n            continue\\n        remaining = resp.headers.get(\\\"X-RateLimit-Remaining\\\")\\n        if remaining is not None and int(remaining) <= 1:\\n            time.sleep(60)                           # avoid hitting the wall mid-batch\\n```\\n\\nFull per-tier, per-category limits: [\u00a72 Rate limiting reference](#2-rate-limiting-reference).\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 2. Rate limiting reference\\n\\n### 2.1 How it works\\n\\n- Limits are enforced **per account (tier)** **and per category**. A `bulk` request and a `standard` request draw from **separate budgets** \u2014 they don't exhaust each other.\\n- Categories are assigned per endpoint: most endpoints are `standard`; bulk record inserts are `bulk`; sync triggers are `sync` (see the [endpoint index](API_REFERENCE.md#endpoint-index)).\\n- Rate-limit headers are returned on **every** response \u2014 including `429` (this was fixed in v2.1; older versions omitted them on `429`).\\n\\n### 2.2 Limits by tier and category\\n\\n| Category | Free tier | Pro tier | Enterprise |\\n|----------|-----------|----------|------------|\\n| **standard** | 100 requests/min \u00b7 10,000/day | 1,000 requests/min \u00b7 unlimited daily | custom |\\n| **bulk** (`POST /datasets/{id}/records`) | **20 requests/min** | not published \u2014 read `X-RateLimit-Limit` | custom |\\n| **sync** (`POST /datasets/{id}/sync`) | not published \u2014 read `X-RateLimit-Limit` | not published \u2014 read `X-RateLimit-Limit` | custom |\\n\\n> Some category/tier combinations don't have published numbers. Make one request in that category and read `X-RateLimit-Limit` from the response \u2014 that is your authoritative limit for the current window. Enterprise customers can request custom limits via support.\\n\\n### 2.3 Response headers\\n\\n| Header | Meaning |\\n|--------|---------|\\n| `X-RateLimit-Limit` | Max requests allowed in the current window (per category) |\\n| `X-RateLimit-Remaining` | Requests left in the current window |\\n| `X-RateLimit-Reset` | Unix timestamp when the window resets |\\n\\n### 2.4 Handling `429` correctly\\n\\n1. **Honor `X-RateLimit-Reset`** \u2014 sleep until that Unix timestamp, don't hammer.\\n2. **Back off with exponential backoff + jitter** for repeated `429`s.\\n3. **Watch `X-RateLimit-Remaining`** proactively and throttle before you hit zero \u2014 don't treat the limit as something to \\\"discover\\\".\\n4. **Don't retry immediately** \u2014 an instant retry consumes another request and extends your lockout.\\n5. **Separate your workers by category**: a bulk-insert worker and a read worker have independent budgets; don't serialize them behind one global semaphore based on the `standard` limit.\\n6. `POST /auth/login` itself returns `429` on too many attempts \u2014 implement token refresh rather than re-logging in every request.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 3. Common migration pitfalls (v2.0 \u2192 v2.2)\\n\\nDrawn from recurring support patterns:\\n\\n| # | Pitfall | What happens | Fix |\\n|---|---------|--------------|-----|\\n| 1 | Keeping API-key auth past v2.1 | `401` after upgrade | Migrate to JWT ([Migration Guide \u00a72](MIGRATION_GUIDE_v2.0_to_v2.2.md#2-authentication-migration-api-keys--jwt)) |\\n| 2 | No token-refresh logic | Works for 1 hour, then everything 401s | Refresh on 401 and retry once; access tokens live 1h, refresh tokens 7d |\\n| 3 | Subscribing to `dataset.deleted` | Webhook never fires | Event doesn't exist; archive fires `dataset.updated` with `archived: true` |\\n| 4 | Assuming `DELETE /datasets/{id}` destroys data | Data \\\"still there\\\" | It's a soft delete \u2014 the dataset is archived, not removed |\\n| 5 | Assuming `DELETE .../records/{record_id}` is soft | Data unexpectedly gone | Record deletes **are** hard deletes |\\n| 6 | `limit` > 100 on list endpoints | Fewer results than expected, or validation error | Max page size is 100; paginate with `page` |\\n| 7 | Sending `filter` unencoded | `400` or ignored filter | `filter` must be **JSON-encoded** |\\n| 8 | Missing `Content-Type: application/json` | `400` on POST/PUT/PATCH | Set the header on all body-carrying requests |\\n| 9 | Dataset names outside 3\u2013100 chars, or duplicates | `400` / `409` | Validate name length client-side; handle `409` (conflict) explicitly |\\n| 10 | > 1000 records per bulk request | `400` | Chunk inserts to \u2264 1000 records |\\n| 11 | Single-record insert loops | Slow, burns through the `bulk` budget | Batch arrays (now 3x faster in v2.2) |\\n| 12 | Treating all endpoints as one rate budget | Unexpected `429` on bulk/sync endpoints | Categories are separate \u2014 see \u00a72 |\\n| 13 | Polling `GET /jobs/{job_id}` in a tight loop | Wasted quota; possible rate limit | Poll with backoff, or use `sync.completed`/`sync.failed` webhooks |\\n| 14 | Syncing with `mode: full` on a schedule | Massive redundant transfers | Use `mode: incremental` (v2.1+); reserve `full` for first run/repairs |\\n| 15 | Parsing the response as a bare payload | Code breaks on error responses | All responses use the `{success, data, error, meta}` envelope |\\n| 16 | Ignoring `error.details` on `400` | Hard-to-debug validation failures | Field-specific messages are in the error details |\\n| 17 | Reporting errors without `request_id` | Slow support turnaround | Always send `meta.request_id` (required for `500`s) |\\n| 18 | Testing against production | Polluted data, quota burn | Sandbox resets daily and is built for experimentation |\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 4. Authentication error diagnostics\\n\\n### 4.1 Quick diagnostic flow\\n\\n```\\n401 received\\n \u251c\u2500 Is an Authorization header present at all?\\n \u2502   \u2514\u2500 No \u2192 add it: Authorization: Bearer <access_token>\\n \u251c\u2500 Is the header well-formed (\\\"Bearer <token>\\\", no stray quotes/spaces)?\\n \u2502   \u2514\u2500 No \u2192 fix the header format\\n \u251c\u2500 Is the token a JWT access token (not an API key)?\\n \u2502   \u2514\u2500 No \u2192 obtain one via POST /auth/login\\n \u251c\u2500 Was the access token issued more than 1 hour ago?\\n \u2502   \u2514\u2500 Yes \u2192 POST /auth/refresh with the refresh_token, then retry\\n \u251c\u2500 Was the refresh token issued more than 7 days ago?\\n \u2502   \u2514\u2500 Yes \u2192 refresh token expired: POST /auth/login again\\n \u251c\u2500 Did you call /auth/logout without a refresh_token body?\\n \u2502   \u2514\u2500 Yes \u2192 that invalidated ALL tokens: log in again\\n \u2514\u2500 Still failing with a token you believe is valid?\\n     \u2514\u2500 Call GET /me with the same token (see 4.2), then contact support\\n        with meta.request_id\\n```\\n\\n### 4.2 Symptom \u2192 cause \u2192 fix\\n\\n| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |\\n|---------|--------------|-----|\\n| `401` on every request, no header sent | Missing `Authorization` header | Add `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` |\\n| `401` with `Bearer <api-key>` | API key sent where a JWT is expected | Login via `POST /auth/login`, use the returned access token |\\n| `401` after ~1 hour of uptime | Access token expired | `POST /auth/refresh`; auto-refresh on 401 + single retry |\\n| `401` from `POST /auth/refresh` (\\\"expired token\\\") | Refresh token older than 7 days (or invalid/revoked) | Re-authenticate with `POST /auth/login` |\\n| `401` after a logout call | `POST /auth/logout` without a `refresh_token` body invalidates **all** tokens | Log in again; always pass `refresh_token` if you only want that session invalidated |\\n| `401` on `POST /auth/login` itself | Invalid credentials \u2014 or too many attempts (`429` also possible) | Check credentials; back off before retrying |\\n| `403` (not `401`) | Authenticated, but not allowed to do that | Request access/permissions \u2014 the token itself is fine |\\n| `401` although `GET /me` succeeds with the same token | Possible platform-side issue | Capture `meta.request_id` and contact support |\\n\\n### 4.3 `401` vs `403` \u2014 which is which\\n\\n- **`401 Unauthorized`** \u2014 *not authenticated*: the request didn't carry a valid token. Fix credentials/tokens.\\n- **`403 Forbidden`** \u2014 *authenticated but not authorized*: the token is valid; the account lacks permission for that resource or action. Fix permissions, not auth.\\n\\n> Note: a permissions problem should surface as `403`. If you receive `401` while the same token successfully calls `GET /me`, treat it as suspect \u2014 verify your token with `GET /me` first, then report the behavior to support with the `meta.request_id` so we can investigate.\\n\\n### 4.4 What to include when contacting support\\n\\n- `meta.request_id` from the failing response (always; required for `500`s)\\n- Timestamp of the request and the endpoint + method\\n- Your tier (Free / Pro / Enterprise)\\n- Which auth method the failing client uses (JWT vs legacy API key) and whether the token was freshly issued or long-lived\\n- For webhook issues: your webhook configuration (`url` + subscribed `events`) and one raw delivery (headers + body) if you received any\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 5. Error-code quick reference\\n\\n| Code | Meaning | Typical trigger | What to do |\\n|------|---------|-----------------|------------|\\n| `400` | Validation failed | Bad body/params; > 1000 records; name length; unencoded filter | Read field-specific messages in the error details |\\n| `401` | Not authenticated | Missing/expired/invalid token | See \u00a74 |\\n| `403` | Forbidden | Valid token, insufficient permission | Request access; don't retry blindly |\\n| `404` | Not found | Wrong ID \u2014 or resource owned by another user | Verify IDs and ownership |\\n| `409` | Conflict | Duplicate dataset name | Rename or adopt the existing resource |\\n| `422` | Business rule violation | Semantically valid but not allowed | Read the error message for the rule |\\n| `429` | Rate limited | Category/tier budget exhausted | Honor `X-RateLimit-Reset`; see \u00a72 |\\n| `500` | Server error | Platform fault | Retry with backoff; report `meta.request_id` |\\n\",\"filePath\":\"/work/output/TROUBLESHOOTING_GUIDE.md\"}", "type": "tool_call"}]

There are **no breaking changes** in this release. 1: # Developer Notes - DataSync API
2: # These are internal notes from the dev team - NOT for external publication
3: # Last updated by multiple contributors
4: 
5: == AUTH STUFF ==
6: We use JWT tokens now. Changed from API keys last sprint (v2.1).
7: Token expires in 1 hour. Refresh tokens last 7 days.
8: Header format: Authorization: Bearer <token>
9: Login endpoint: POST /auth/login - takes email+password, returns tokens
10: Refresh: POST /auth/refresh - takes refresh_token in body
11: 
12: BUG: Sometimes 401 returns instead of 403 when token valid but perms wrong
13: TODO: Fix in next sprint (JIRA-4521)
14: 
15: == DATA ENDPOINTS ==
16: 
17: /datasets - GET list all datasets for user
18: params: page (default 1), limit (default 20, max 100), status (active|archived|all)
19: returns array of dataset objects
20: 
21: /datasets/{id} - GET single dataset
22: 404 if not found or not owned by user
23: 
24: /datasets - POST create new dataset
25: body: { name: string (required, 3-100 chars), description: string (optional), tags: array }
26: returns created dataset with id
27: 
28: /datasets/{id} - PUT update dataset
29: same body as POST but all fields optional
30: returns updated dataset
31: 
32: /datasets/{id} - DELETE soft delete (sets archived flag)
33: returns 204 no content
34: 
35: /datasets/{id}/records - GET records in dataset
36: pagination same as /datasets list
37: params: sort (field name), order (asc|desc), filter (JSON encoded query)
38: 
39: /datasets/{id}/records - POST add record(s)
40: body can be single object or array for bulk insert
41: max 1000 records per request
42: 
43: /datasets/{id}/records/{record_id} - PATCH update single record
44: body: partial record object
45: 
46: /datasets/{id}/sync - POST trigger sync with external source
47: body: { source_id: string, mode: "full"|"incremental" }
48: returns job_id for async tracking
49: 
50: /jobs/{job_id} - GET check job status
51: response: { status: "pending"|"running"|"completed"|"failed", progress: 0-100, error: string|null }
52: 
53: == ERROR CODES ==
54: 
55: 400 - bad request (validation failed) - body has "errors" array with field-specific messages
56: 401 - not authenticated
57: 403 - forbidden (authenticated but not authorized)
58: 404 - not found
59: 409 - conflict (e.g., duplicate name)
60: 422 - unprocessable entity (business rule violation)
61: 429 - rate limited (100 req/min for free tier, 1000 for pro)
62: 500 - server error (we log these, include request_id in response for support)
63: 
64: == RESPONSE FORMAT ==
65: 
66: All responses wrapped:
67: {
68:   "success": true|false,
69:   "data": <payload>|null,
70:   "error": null|{ "code": "ERR_CODE", "message": "Human readable", "details": {} },
71:   "meta": { "request_id": "uuid", "timestamp": "ISO8601" }
72: }
73: 
74: == WEBHOOKS (v2.2 feature) ==
75: 
76: POST /webhooks - create webhook
77: body: { url: string, events: ["dataset.created", "dataset.updated", "sync.completed", "sync.failed"], secret: string (optional, for HMAC signing) }
78: 
79: GET /webhooks - list webhooks
80: DELETE /webhooks/{id} - remove webhook
81: 
82: Webhook payload:
83: {
84:   "event": "event.type",
85:   "timestamp": "ISO8601",
86:   "data": { <event specific> }
87: }
88: 
89: If secret provided, we send X-Webhook-Signature header with HMAC-SHA256 of body
90: 
91: == RATE LIMITS ==
92: 
93: Free tier: 100 requests/minute, 10000/day
94: Pro tier: 1000 requests/minute, unlimited daily
95: Enterprise: custom
96: 
97: Headers returned:
98: X-RateLimit-Limit: <max>
99: X-RateLimit-Remaining: <remaining>
100: X-RateLimit-Reset: <unix timestamp>
101: 
102: == SDK notes ==
103: 
104: Python SDK wraps all this, handles auth refresh automatically
105: JS SDK in beta - dont document yet
106: Java SDK abandoned - dont mention
107: 
108: == CHANGELOG snippets ==
109: 
110: v2.2.0 (2024-12-15)
111: - Added webhooks
112: - Fixed: sync jobs sometimes stuck in "running"
113: - Improved: bulk insert now 3x faster
114: 
115: v2.1.0 (2024-11-01)
116: - BREAKING: Switched to JWT auth (API keys deprecated, removed in v3)
117: - Added incremental sync mode
118: - Fixed: rate limit headers missing on 429 responses
119: 
120: v2.0.0 (2024-09-15)
121: - Complete rewrite
122: - New endpoint structure
123: - Added job queue for async operations
124: 
125: == MISC ==
126: 
127: Base URL: https://api.datasync.io/v2
128: Sandbox: https://sandbox.api.datasync.io/v2 (resets daily, fake data ok)
129: 
130: Content-Type must be application/json for all POST/PUT/PATCH
131: 
132: CORS enabled for *.datasync.io domains, customers can request whitelist
133: 
134: OpenAPI spec is auto-generated but has bugs - dont use directly, needs manual cleanup

Either way, **all API-key usage must end before v3** — the question is only *when* you move.\n\n| Your situation | Recommendation |\n|----------------|----------------|\n| New integration starting today | **JWT only.** Never build on deprecated auth. |\n| Single service, credentials in central config/secret store | **Migrate now.** Effort is small: add login + refresh logic, swap the header. |\n| Services cannot yet handle a 1-hour token expiry (no refresh logic) | **Stay on API keys short-term**, add refresh handling on a staging branch, then cut over. |\n| Large fleet (dozens of microservices) sharing one credential | **Phased migration** (see §2.5): introduce a central token broker, migrate services incrementally, keep API keys only for stragglers until v3. |\n| Security/compliance requires short-lived credentials | **Migrate now.** 1-hour access tokens are strictly better than never-expiring keys. |\n| Automation calls `GET/POST /me/api-keys` to manage keys | **Plan replacement now.** These endpoints are deprecated and will disappear in v3; key management will not be the auth path going forward. |\n\n**Rule of thumb:** if your code treats its credential as *permanent*, you will break when v3 removes API keys. Migrating early means one deliberate change now instead of an emergency later.\n\n### 2.4 Before/after: authentication code\n\n**Before (v2.0 — static API key, sent on every request, never expires):**\n\n```python\n# v2.0 pattern (pseudocode). Incremental sync (added in v2.1 — commonly missed)\n\nMany v2.0-era integrations never noticed that `POST /datasets/{id}/sync` accepts a **`mode`** parameter:\n\n| Mode | Behavior |\n|------|----------|\n| `full` (default) | Re-syncs the entire external source into the dataset |\n| `incremental` | Transfers only changes since the last successful sync |\n\nSync is asynchronous: the call returns `202` with a `job_id`; track it via `GET /jobs/{job_id}` (`status`: `pending|running|completed|failed`, `progress`: 0–100, `error`).
